subject.title: Feature: Streaming TTS pipeline for voice calls (sentence-level LLM→TTS→audio)

question: Should classic Voice Call gain a supported provider-generic sentence/audio streaming contract, and which initial TTS-provider plus carrier combination should define that contract?
rationale: The implementation changes shared speech and embedded-agent boundaries plus user-visible partial-playback recovery semantics; code inspection cannot safely choose that permanent API and rollout policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor additive streaming contract
options.body: Add optional incremental text and telephony-audio APIs, start with one proven provider/carrier combination, and retain the existing buffered path for unsupported providers and pre-audio failures.

options.title: Use realtime voice only
options.body: Keep classic STT-to-agent-to-TTS deliberately buffered and direct low-latency users to the separate OpenAI or Gemini full-duplex realtime architecture.

options.title: Defer pending narrower design
options.body: Keep the issue canonical but require a smaller API proposal and live carrier benchmark before accepting implementation work.

recommendation.title: Sponsor additive streaming contract
recommendation.body: Add optional incremental text and telephony-audio APIs, start with one proven provider/carrier combination, and retain the existing buffered path for unsupported providers and pre-audio failures.

likelyOwner.reason: The history shows the broadest ownership across Voice Call response generation, telephony playback, realtime architecture, and the recent early-delivery merge boundary.
